title: BPR: Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
claim: Pairwise learning directly optimizes a user's preference for observed positives over sampled alternatives.
cautions: Negative sampling policy materially changes the learned objective.

title: From RankNet to LambdaRank to LambdaMART
claim: Lambda-weighted ranking gradients emphasize swaps that most affect ranking metrics such as NDCG.
cautions: Query or user groups must be constructed exactly and kept intact.

title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
claim: Target-aware attention can activate the parts of a user's behavior history most relevant to the candidate item.
cautions: History construction must be causal to prevent future leakage.

title: Deep Interest Evolution Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
claim: Interest representations can evolve over a behavior sequence and condition on the target item.
cautions: Sequence preprocessing and recurrent training raise implementation cost.

title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
claim: Causal self-attention provides an efficient sequential recommendation inductive bias.
cautions: Next-item retrieval objectives are not identical to within-impression long-view ranking.

title: Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts
claim: Task-specific gates over shared experts can model related outcomes while reducing harmful parameter sharing.
cautions: Auxiliary labels can cause negative transfer and must be ablated.

title: AIDE: AI-Driven Exploration in the Space of Code
claim: ML engineering can be organized as tree search over code solutions with explicit improvement and debugging branches.
cautions: The evaluator and data boundaries must remain outside model-authored code.

title: MLEvolve: Progressive Learning for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
claim: Retrospective memory and cross-branch fusion can retain useful discoveries across an iterative ML search.
cautions: Experiment history is not formal gradient-based meta-learning.

title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
claim: End-to-end ML agents can be evaluated through executable competition tasks and held-out performance.
cautions: Leaderboard score alone does not capture robustness or intervention count.

title: Is Meta-Learning the Right Approach for the Cold-Start Problem in Recommender Systems?
claim: Well-tuned conventional deep models can match or outperform several meta-learning cold-start approaches.
cautions: Do not introduce task-level meta-learning without evidence of a real adaptation bottleneck.
